cards.text: It's the second year of King Darius, the first day of the sixth month. The word of the LORD comes through Haggai the prophet to two leaders: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. The LORD of Hosts starts by repeating what these people have been saying about rebuilding the house of the LORD.

cards.question: What are the people saying about rebuilding the house of the LORD?

answers.text: The time has not yet come
The work is too hard for us
We have no stones to build with

cards.text: Friend, "not yet" is the snooze button talking, and I KNOW that button, because I've hit it so hard it started hitting BACK. Then the word of the LORD comes through Haggai again, and this time it's a question.

cards.question: God asks: is it time for the people to live in their ___ houses while His house lies in ruins?

cards.text: Paneled walls at home and ruins at the LORD's house is like me polishing my gold base till it GLOWS while the bakery oven sits there in PIECES. Now the LORD of Hosts says, 'Consider carefully your ways.'

cards.question: God tells the people they have planted much and harvested much.

cards.text: Planted much, harvested LITTLE. And God keeps going: 'You eat but never have enough. You drink but never have your fill.'

cards.question: God says that when the people put on clothes, they finally get warm.

cards.text: Nope, never warm either, and their paychecks have it rough too. God says, 'You earn wages to put into a bag pierced through.'

cards.question: God says the people put their wages into a bag pierced through. What's the picture?

answers.text: Their money slips away as fast as it comes in
Thieves keep breaking in and taking their money
They hide their money away and forget about it

cards.text: You know this one, friend: payday hits, and two days later you're staring at your account like, WHERE did it GO? Then God says it again, same words: 'Consider carefully your ways.'
And then come the instructions, plain as a recipe card: 'Go up into the hills, bring down lumber, and build the house'

cards.question: Why does God tell the people to build His house?

answers.text: So He may take pleasure in it and be glorified
So the priests can live in it and be safe
So the governor can rule from it in peace

cards.text: Then God says, 'You expected much, but behold, it amounted to little.' And He tells them what happened to what they did bring home.

cards.question: God says He Himself blew away what the people brought home.
God asks why it all came to so little. His answer: His house still lies in ruins, while each of them is busy with his own ___.

cards.text: Busy, busy, BUSY, friend, just not on the LORD's house. Then God says the heavens have withheld their dew and the earth has withheld its crops.

cards.question: God says the heavens have withheld their dew on account of the people.
The LORD says He has summoned a ___ on the fields and on the mountains.

cards.text: That drought hits the grain, the new wine, the oil, man and beast, and all the labor of their hands. We'll pause the ovens right there, friend, because the LORD isn't done talking yet.
